text:
Kai: Heads-up: got a ticket from finance — three customers reported unexpected rate-limit errors + bill spikes after the "Set account default API version" flip. Anyone digging?
Ellen: Which customers? do we have traces?
Kai: `gridworks`, `verdant`, `sprintly`. Traces show requests without X-Redwood-Client-Version header; routing honored account default -> v2 instances. Quota service used existing route quota keys which were tied to old pinned_version -> mismatch.
Marta: TL;DR: routing and quota-key materialization are out of sync when console flips account default. We infer served version at request time for routing, but quota keys were not backfilled; created new smaller v2 buckets = throttles.
DevOpsBot: alert created: infra/tenant_version_quota_mismatch severity=high. Owner: @Ishan.
Ishan: Immediate mitigation idea: proxy can add `X-Redwood-Quota-Key: route:<id>:pinned:v1` for a short grace when console flips default. That preserves quota bucket mapping while routing to v2. Console can toggle that per-tenant for 24h.
Ellen: add visibility first: emit `X-Redwood-Served-Version` response header so customers and our logs can see which variant served the request. Also add structured audit log when console default changes listing affected routes and previous pinned_version.
Kai: agree. UX note: console toggle currently says "Set default" only. We should show a modal: "This will change routing for N routes and may rekey quotas for older routes. Confirm to proceed" with an option to preview affected routes.
Marta: long-term: introduce explicit `served_version` column on route records. Routing reads served_version if present, else falls back to header->route pin->account default. Quota-key lookup uses the materialized served_version. When default flips, do NOT mutate served_version for existing routes unless running a migration job. New routes get current default.
Ishan: migration job should be opt-in with audit trail and an auto-rollback window. But given customers already hit billing spikes, we should provide a one-click console migration with a staged pace (50 tenants/min) and email notice.
Ellen: telemetry alert draft (PromQL): `sum by(tenant,version) (increase(tokens_used[15m])) / sum by(tenant) (increase(tokens_used[15m])) > 0.5 and increase(billing_cost[1h]) > 0.2 * increase(billing_cost[24h])`. Fire when both true.
Marta: Also add a safeguard: block account-default flips for any tenant that had >30% traffic change in last 24h or any ongoing migration.
Ishan: I'll implement the proxy header shim + alert ownership. Kai, can you own the console modal and the per-tenant override button?
Kai: yup. I'll also add an urgency CTA in modal: "If you see unexpected rate limits after flipping defaults, use this override to revert quotas without changing routing."
Ellen: Docs: add note to API compatibility page about "default version flips may not rekey quotas automatically" and list recovery steps (override header, contact support, request migration).
DevOpsBot: created feature-flag `console.default_version_migration_shim` owner=@Ishan.
Marta: action items: Ishan -> proxy shim + alert; Kai -> console modal + override; Ellen -> response header + docs + audit log; Marta -> design migration job and backpressure plan. We'll canary flag to 3% accounts then ramp.
Ishan: one more ops constraint: throttle migration at 60 tenants/min and ensure idempotency using migration id.
Kai: thanks. If anyone sees more billing anomalies, post in #billing and ping me. I'll create a ticket and link here.
_notes: Slack-style eng-platform thread about an account-level console default API version flip that caused routing vs quota key mismatches, producing rate limits and billing spikes. Conversation includes a short mitigation (proxy shim header), telemetry PromQL, console UX changes, migration job plan, and feature-flag canary rollout.
